messages.text: Shop···· Received the 3 miners, two are up and running, the third won’t hash and has a warning pop up saying Current Protection. I’ve tried it on multiple outlets and get the same message.

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, Sarah passed this over to me.

"Current Protection" usually points at the power stage, but the exact meaning changes by model and firmware, so I do not want to guess it.

Two things to start:

1. Which model is the third unit (Harlo B30, Hammer DC02 / DC06 / DC08, NerdQX, Nexus, other)?
2. A photo or screenshot of the screen showing the warning, plus the firmware version from the web UI if you can reach it.

With those I will look the code up for that exact model and firmware and tell you where the answer comes from.
Searched the web · NerdQaxe "Current Protection" "Guru Meditation" esp-miner er
Searched the web · esp-miner "CURRENT PROTECTION" BM1370 overcurrent TPS error

Thanks, I opened the photo. It shows a NerdQaxe++ (BM1370) at 192.168.1.158, "CURRENT PROTECTION, Guru Meditation #51A00000", 0.0 GH/s, 35 C, 0.062 W. So the board is trimming the ASIC rail off before it ever starts hashing.

What that code is, not from memory: on the Nerd* boards it is the firmware current limit on the TPS voltage regulator tripping. 
On the NerdOctaxe Gamma it was a known firmware bug on v1.0.35 and below, where the TPS53647 limit was set too low and got reached in normal conditions, fixed by raising the limit in v1.0.36
 (powermining.io). 
On the NerdQaxe++ specifically, firmware from V1.0.35 enforces a 100A current limit
 (magicminer.cc). The same trip also happens for real when the power supply cannot hold up, or when the TPS itself is faulty.

Two checks, in this order:

1. Power supply swap. Unplug the faulty unit, take the power brick from one of the two units that are hashing fine and run the faulty one on it. Does the same message come back? This is the fastest way to separate a weak brick from a board fault, and trying different wall outlets does not test it.
2. While you are there, tell me the firmware version shown under Settings in the web UI at 192.168.1.158, and whether frequency and core voltage are at stock or were changed.

Send me the result of the brick swap and the firmware version and I will take it from there.
I have logged what we have so far. Send me those two things (does it still trip on a known-good brick, and the firmware version) and we will keep going from there.
Yes, have tried it over the past 2 days. Same message when trying it with a known good brick. Looking at the Settings page: v1.1.0.1
*(Verdict recorded as defective; chat handed back to Sarah, no reply from me.)*
